title: Girl Reading a Letter at an Open Window
source: Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister, Staatliche Kunstsammlungen Dresden (public domain). Wikimedia Commons file: VermeerGirlWindowCupid.jpg (1580 x 2058 px, restored state with the Cupid on the back wall)
caption: A love letter, an open window, and a secret painted over on the wall behind her for centuries. #loveletter #cupid #vermeer #masterpiece #hiddendetails
_verify: VERIFIED, Wikipedia EN (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Girl_Reading_a_Letter_at_an_Open_Window): Vermeer, c. 1657-1659, oil on canvas, 83 x 64.5 cm, Dresden since 1742 (bought as a Rembrandt); window reflects the girl in its lower right quadrant; tasselled curtain masks a quarter of the room in the right foreground; fruit in a tilted bowl, a peach cut in half; Schneider reads the fruit as 'a symbol of extramarital relations'; restored 2018-2021; Cupid resembles a Van Everdingen painting; overpainted wall per Wikipedia 'late 18th century' (not used, other sources only say decades after his death).

VERIFIED, CODART (codart.nl/?p=85374): 1979 X-ray revealed the naked Cupid, published 1982; 'scientists assumed that Vermeer had rejected the Cupid image and painted over the back wall of the room himself'; new tests (X-ray, infrared, microscopy, paint samples at the Dresden Academy of Fine Arts, 2017 XRF scan with the Rijksmuseum) show the overpaint was applied decades later, 'most certainly after his death'; overpaint removed with a scalpel.

VERIFIED, Smithsonian (smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/restoration-reveals-long-lost-cupid-painted-over-after-vermeers-death-180972143/): 'a layer of dirt above the original varnish on the Cupid' (Uta Neidhardt), so the Cupid was exposed for decades before being covered; same Cupid as in A Young Woman Standing at a Virginal (National Gallery, London); widow's 1676 inventory lists 'a Cupid'.

VERIFIED, designboom (designboom.com/art/vermeer-girl-reading-a-letter-at-the-open-window-restored-08-26-2021/) and finestresullarte.info: restoration 2017 to early 2021; Cupid with bow, arrows and two masks, stepping on disguise masks, read as sincere love overcoming deceit; shown restored in Dresden from 10 Sept 2021.
INTERPRETATION, flagged: 'some read' the fruit as a hint of forbidden love (one scholar, Schneider). The letter being a love letter is the usual reading, strengthened by the Cupid, not documented.

BEFORE STATE (text only): for about two and a half centuries the wall behind her looked bare (The Art Newspaper headline: hidden 'after two and a half centuries'). The renderer uses only the restored image; slide boxes are on the restored state.
Focus boxes estimated from the contact sheet; re-tune on the real image (reflection in the glass on slide 3 and the masks at Cupid's feet on slide 8 are the uncertain ones).
COVER: framed on the girl and window (focus on slide 0) so the restored Cupid is not visible on the cover/thumbnail; the reveal stays on slide 6.

slides.headline: For centuries, this wall hid a secret
slides.sub: Johannes Vermeer, Girl Reading a Letter at an Open Window, c. 1657-1659

slides.headline: A quiet moment
slides.text: A young woman reads a letter by an open window. For centuries, the wall behind her looked bare and calm. But it wasn't always.

slides.headline: Her reflection
slides.text: First, look at the glass: her face floats faintly in the open window, a second self lost in the same words. Who wrote to her?

slides.headline: Spilled fruit
slides.text: Below, fruit tumbles from a tilted bowl, a peach cut open beside it. Some read it as a hint of forbidden love.

slides.headline: A curtain pulled aside
slides.text: A heavy curtain hangs in front, as if we were peeking into a private moment. And then, in 1979, an X-ray peeked deeper.

slides.headline: The hidden Cupid
slides.text: Under the bare wall: a painting of a naked Cupid. For decades experts assumed Vermeer had changed his mind and painted it out himself.

slides.headline: Not Vermeer's hand
slides.text: But a restoration begun in 2017 proved otherwise: someone else covered it decades after Vermeer's death. So conservators scraped it off, with a scalpel.

slides.headline: Love beats deceit
slides.text: Revealed in 2021, Cupid stands over masks lying on the floor: true love defeating deceit. Suddenly, there's no doubt what the letter is about.

slides.headline: Which do you prefer?
slides.text: The same Cupid hangs in another Vermeer, in London. Here he was hidden for centuries. Empty wall or Cupid: which version do you prefer?
